newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian rupiah stable in moderate late trading.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian rupiah stable in moderate late trading.

text.p: The Indonesian rupiah was stable against the dollar in late Friday trading, dealers said.
They said some Singapore operators were seen trying to push the market when Jakarta operators went out for lunch.
"The attempts failed as there was no follow-through. There was no momentum at all," one U.S. bank dealer said.
One local bank dealer said there was no fresh rumours in the market to support the dollar's uptrend, causing it to retreat after edging to the day's high of 2,321.0 at midday.
Spot rupiah was last at 2,319.0/21.0 at 0850 GMT against an opening of 2,318.0/20.0.
Tomorrow and today rupiah closed at 2,319.0/19.5 and 2,315.0/16.0, respectively.

The local bank dealer said operators would tend to go short on dollars if it was not for the weekend. He said the brief upturn of the dollar was also partly due to short-covering as operators did not want to be left short at the weekend.
Dealers said swap rates had stabilised after edging up slightly in the morning on a tight liquidity condition.
Overnight money had eased to 12.0 percent late in the afternoon after hitting the day's high of 28.0/30.0 percent.
Dealers said short-dated swap rates had also eased.
Overnight swap closed at 2.00/2.35. Tom/next was at 0.48/0.55 and spot/next at 0.49/0.54 points.
"Sentiment is a bit neutral at present. I think people will focus more on the liquidity issue next week due to the approaching month-end," another foreign bank dealer said.
He said the dollar-rupiah rate was expected to range between 2,317.0 and 2,322.0 on Monday.
The rupiah was jolted briefly on Thursday following market rumours over the health of President Suharto.
But the currency recovered quickly late in the afternoon as palace officials said the rumours were unfounded.
The rupiah staged a strong recovery in New York overnight which carried forward to the Jakarta opening.
One-month swap was quoted at 15.25/15.75, two at 31.5/33.0, three at 46.00/46.75 and six at 95.0/96.5 points.
Bank Indonesia raised its intervention rate by one point to 2,312/2,504 and the conversion rate also by one point to 2,312/2,360 on Friday.
